subject: microbiology
title: Coxiella burnetii, Q Fever and Chlamydia trachomatis

steps.tx: **Coxiella burnetii** is a highly infectious obligate intracellular bacterium that forms a resistant small cell variant in animal birth products, manure and dust. Inhalation causes **Q fever**, often after exposure to sheep, goats or cattle parturition. The acute illness usually produces fever, headache, myalgia, hepatitis or atypical pneumonia. Infective dose can be extremely low, making it a major laboratory biosafety organism.
steps.say: Q fever begins by inhaling Coxiella from birth products and contaminated farm dust.

left.title: Exposure clues
points: Lambing, kidding or calving
Abattoir and veterinary work
Manure, straw and farm dust
Windborne spread beyond immediate animal contact

right.title: Resistance
points: Small cell variant resists drying
Survives in the environment for long periods
Routine culture is dangerous and unnecessary
BSL 3 containment for propagation

steps.tx: Coxiella undergoes **phase variation**: phase I organisms with full lipopolysaccharide are highly virulent, while phase II forms arise after passage and have truncated lipopolysaccharide. Serology exploits this distinction. Acute Q fever usually shows dominant phase II IgG, whereas chronic Q fever develops very high phase I IgG, often in endocarditis or vascular infection. Phase terminology therefore describes antigenic form, not illness week.
steps.say: High phase I IgG points toward chronic Q fever; dominant phase II response fits acute disease.

left.title: Acute Q fever
points: Self limited febrile illness in many cases
Hepatitis or pneumonia pattern
Phase II IgG and IgM response
Blood PCR can help before seroconversion

right.title: Chronic Q fever
points: Culture negative endocarditis is classic
Vascular graft or aneurysm infection
High phase I IgG titre
Needs prolonged doxycycline plus hydroxychloroquine

steps.tx: Chronic Q fever can remain silent until **prosthetic valve endocarditis**, infected aneurysm or pregnancy complications occur. Echocardiography may underestimate vegetations, so PET CT is often useful. Treatment is prolonged because Coxiella persists in acidic intracellular vacuoles; hydroxychloroquine raises vacuolar pH and improves doxycycline activity. Serologic and clinical monitoring continue long after symptoms resolve.
steps.say: Chronic Q fever needs prolonged combination therapy guided by phase I antibody trends.

left.title: Risk settings
points: Prosthetic or damaged heart valves
Vascular grafts and aneurysms
Immunosuppression
Pregnancy can trigger relapse risk

right.title: Monitoring
points: Phase I IgG should fall with control
PET CT finds vascular and valve foci
Drug levels and eye monitoring may be needed
Relapse can occur after premature cessation

steps.tx: **Chlamydia trachomatis** is another obligate intracellular organism but follows a biphasic developmental cycle. The infectious elementary body enters epithelial cells and converts into the replicating reticulate body within an inclusion. Serovars A to C cause trachoma, D to K cause genital and neonatal infection, and L1 to L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum. Diagnosis generally uses nucleic acid amplification testing rather than culture.
steps.say: Trachoma, genital chlamydia and LGV differ mainly by C trachomatis serovar and tissue invasion.

left.title: Serovar groups
points: A to C: trachoma
D to K: cervicitis, urethritis, PID and neonatal disease
L1 to L3: invasive lymphogranuloma venereum
All share elementary and reticulate body cycle

right.title: Typical tests
points: NAAT from urine or genital swab
Rectal and pharyngeal NAAT where validated
Culture reserved for special legal or research cases
Point of care assays still require quality assessment

steps.tx: Genital **C trachomatis** infection is often asymptomatic but can cause cervicitis, urethritis, pelvic inflammatory disease, tubal infertility, ectopic pregnancy, epididymitis and reactive arthritis. Screening sexually active young people and treating partners prevents reinfection and complications. A NAAT positive result should prompt testing for gonorrhoea, syphilis and HIV, partner notification, abstinence until treatment completion and retesting for reinfection.
steps.say: Silent chlamydia can still scar fallopian tubes, so screening and partner therapy are prevention.

left.title: Consequences
points: Pelvic inflammatory disease
Tubal factor infertility
Ectopic pregnancy risk
Increased HIV acquisition and transmission risk

right.title: Control steps
points: Test symptomatic patients and risk groups
Treat partners from the lookback interval
Avoid sex until therapy and partner treatment complete
Retest at about three months for reinfection

steps.tx: **Trachoma** remains a blinding disease of poverty and limited water access. Repeated childhood C trachomatis infection causes follicular conjunctivitis, conjunctival scarring, entropion and trichiasis, then corneal opacity. The SAFE strategy combines surgery for trichiasis, antibiotics such as mass azithromycin, facial cleanliness and environmental improvement. A single exposure matters less than the cycle of reinfection in crowded households.
steps.say: Trachoma blinds through repeated infections, scarring and inward turning lashes abrading the cornea.
